ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the figure is a schematic map of the Bohai Rim region, marking cities such as Beijing, Tianjin, Dalian, Jinan, and Qingdao, as well as resource points such as iron ore, petroleum, coal, sea salt, and natural gas. In the legend there are two types of linear elements, highways and railways, and in the figure multiple highways and railways connect cities such as the Beijing—Tianjin—Tangshan area, the Liaoning coast, and the Shandong Peninsula, forming an obvious direction of urban linkage. Then reason: the question asks what lines the “city aggregation axes” in urbanization often rely on to form; from the figure, the aggregation and extension between cities mainly unfold along transportation lines such as highways and railways, so it should be summarized as forming relying on main transportation trunk lines.
